title: Volume Explorer — Rectangular Prisms
objectives: Find the volume of the blue rectangular prism (5×3×4)
Fill the empty pool with blocks and count them
Calculate the volume of the L-block

title: Area & Surface Area
objectives: Find the area of the base layer (blue prism)
Count the layers to find the height
Calculate the volume using Area × Height
Compare two prisms with the same volume but different shapes

title: Build Challenge — Design Your Dream Room
objectives: Build a room with walls 4 blocks high
Calculate the interior volume of your room
Add a second room connected to the first
Find the total volume of both rooms combined

title: Real-World Volume — Packing & Shipping
objectives: Find how many small boxes fit in the shipping container
Calculate the wasted space in a partially filled crate
Design a package that holds exactly 36 cubic units

title: The Geometry Garden — A Place to Discover
objectives: Walk the path through the garden
Use M to measure anything that interests you
Notice: which structures have the same volume but different shapes?
Find the hidden structure at the end of the path

title: Composite Volume — Breaking Apart & Combining
objectives: Decompose the T-shape into 2 rectangular prisms
Calculate each part’s volume and find the total
Solve the step pyramid by counting layer volumes
Design your own composite shape with exactly 50 cubic units

title: Fractional Dimensions — Beyond Whole Numbers
objectives: Compare a 4×3×2 prism to a 4×3×2.5 prism
Calculate volume when one dimension is a fraction
Understand that volume can be a non-whole number
Estimate the volume of a partially filled container

title: Volume Estimation — Think Before You Count
objectives: Estimate each structure’s volume BEFORE measuring
Use the reference cube (1 block) to calibrate your estimates
See how close your estimates are to the actual volumes
Estimation is a skill — it gets better with practice!

title: Fraction Builder — Parts of a Whole
objectives: Place two half-blocks side by side — do they equal one whole cube?
Build a structure using only half-blocks. What’s its volume?
Combine cubes and half-blocks to make exactly 3½ cubic units
Use the ◢ shape selector to switch between cube, half, and quarter shapes

title: Base 10 Place Value — Building Numbers in 3D
objectives: Identify units (1), tens (10), and hundreds (100) blocks
Build the number 234 using base-10 blocks
Compare two numbers by counting their blocks
Understand that 10 ones = 1 ten, 10 tens = 1 hundred

title: Volume Fluency Maze — Measure to Navigate
objectives: Measure each structure at a junction to find its volume
Choose the path labeled with the correct answer
Reach the golden finish platform at the end
Complete the maze as fast as you can!
